content:
Using all 16-divisor patterns, the smallest three-digit candidates below \(168\) are only
\[
2^3\cdot 3\cdot 5=120,\qquad 2^3\cdot 3\cdot 7=168.
\]
Other patterns start at \(210\) or higher.

For a five-digit multiple \(N=2014k\), we have \(k=5,\dots,49\), and
\[
\overline{CDE}=2014k \pmod{1000}=14k.
\]
For \(k=5,\dots,11\), the values are
\[
70,84,98,112,126,140,154,
\]
none of which has 16 factors. For \(k=12\),
\[
\overline{CDE}=14\cdot 12=168=2^3\cdot 3\cdot 7,
\]
which has
\[
(3+1)(1+1)(1+1)=16
\]
factors.

Thus the smallest number is
\[
2014\cdot 12=24168.
\]
\[
\boxed{24168}
\]
